title.source: Section check: Evidence and early connections
title.back: Section check: Evidence and connections in the early era

intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 1–3. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.note: "Take your time" is ไม่ต้องรีบ. The same intro, middle and low results are used in all four checks; they should match the wording the Our World checks (content/th/quizzes/) end up with.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 1–3. No need to hurry. You can go back to the lessons and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.source: You look at the photo of the Ban Chiang pot. You say, "It has painted swirls." Which word fits what you said?
questions.0.question.note: "painted swirls" was ลายก้นหอยที่วาดด้วยสี. Second pass: now ลายก้นหอยเขียนสี, the wording SAT01 uses (and Thai museum texts); flag removed. The quiz's รูปถ่าย/รูป is now ภาพถ่าย/ภาพ throughout, as in the lessons.
questions.0.question.back: You look at a photo of a Ban Chiang pot and say, "This pot has painted spirals." Which word matches what you said?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: An inference, an idea to test
questions.0.options.0.text.note: Options keep the English "word, short meaning" shape as "word คือ meaning" (no commas in Thai). Check they still read as three parallel choices.
questions.0.options.0.text.back: Inference: an idea that needs testing

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. An inference is an idea that explains what you see. You can see the swirls, so this is an observation. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. An inference is an idea that explains what you see. You can see the spirals, so it is an observation. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: An observation, a thing you see

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The swirls are there in the photo. You can see them, so this is an observation.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The spirals really are in the photo. You can see them, so it is an observation.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: Context, where the pot was found
questions.0.options.2.text.back: Context: the place where this pot was found

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Context is where a find lay in the ground and what was near it. The photo does not show that. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Context is the position where something was found in the ground, and the things nearby. The photo does not show this. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.1.stimulus.title.source: A made-up find from a made-up dig
questions.1.stimulus.title.back: A made-up find from a made-up excavation

questions.1.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. At the made-up site of Vessa, a team digs up a clay bowl with painted lines. It lay in a grave, next to a bronze ring. A student writes, "The owner of this bowl was a farmer."
questions.1.stimulus.body.note: "farmer" is ชาวนา (rice farmer), the everyday word; เกษตรกร is more general but more formal. "student" in a made-up example is นักเรียน (not ผู้เรียน, which is the platform's word for the learner).
questions.1.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. At a made-up excavation site called Vessa, a team dug up a clay bowl with painted lines. The bowl was in a grave, next to a bronze ring. A student wrote, "The owner of this bowl was a farmer."

questions.1.question.source: What does the student need before they can say this?
questions.1.question.back: What does the student need first before saying this?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: More evidence than the bowl alone

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A bowl cannot tell us what its owner did. Other finds and records might help, and the answer may stay unsure.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. The bowl cannot tell what work the owner did. Other finds and written records might help, and the answer might still be uncertain.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: Nothing, as the painted lines prove it
questions.1.options.1.text.back: Nothing. The painted lines prove it.

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The lines show that someone painted the bowl. They do not show what its owner did. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The lines say someone painted a pattern on the bowl, but not what work the owner did. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: A clearer photo of the painted lines
questions.1.options.2.text.back: A clearer photo of the painted lines

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A clearer photo still shows only the bowl. It cannot show who owned it. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A clearer picture still shows only the bowl. It cannot tell who owned it. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.2.question.source: Look at the 2015 photo of the balangay planks. Which claim does it support?
questions.2.question.note: balangay = บาลังไกย์. Second pass: checked, this is SAT02's glossary word (and SAT12 now matches); flag removed.
questions.2.question.back: Look at the photo of the balangay boat planks taken in 2015. Which claim does this photo support?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: The boat sailed from Butuan to China
questions.2.options.0.text.back: This boat sailed from Butuan to China.

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The photo shows planks, not a route. It cannot show where the boat went. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. This photo shows planks, not a route, so it cannot tell where the boat went. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Nobody found the pottery inside a boat. The pottery is a different find. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. No one found pottery in the boat. The pottery is a different find. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: People in Butuan built plank boats
questions.2.options.2.text.back: People in Butuan built boats from planks.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. You can see the wooden planks and the holes along them. They show how people built boats.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. You can see the planks and the holes lined up along the wood. These show how people built boats.

questions.3.question.source: On the lesson's map, the lines from Butuan to other places are dashed. Why?
questions.3.question.back: On the lesson's map, the lines from Butuan to other places are dashed. Why?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: They show links that were possible

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The boats and the imported pottery are clues to links by sea. But no source shows one exact trip.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. The boats and imported pottery are clues to sea connections, but no source shows any one exact journey.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: They show the exact route of one boat
questions.3.options.1.text.back: The lines show the exact route of one boat.

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. No source tells us where the Butuan boats sailed. The lines show only possible links. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. No source says where Butuan's boats sailed. These lines show only possible connections. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: They show trips that boats made each year
questions.3.options.2.text.back: The lines show a journey boats made every year.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The sources do not say how often anyone sailed. The lines show only possible links. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The sources do not say how often people sailed. These lines show only possible connections. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.4.question.source: The map of Melaka is dated 1604. Which time can it help you study?
questions.4.question.back: The map of Melaka is dated 1604. Which time can this map help you study?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: Melaka in the 1400s, under the sultanate
questions.4.options.0.text.note: "the 1400s" is ช่วงปี 1400 ถึง 1499, as KEY_TERMS says; this makes the wrong option longer than the others (allowed) and is a little heavy. A reviewer may prefer ช่วงปี 1400 กว่า. Second pass: kept; this is the course's style for one century (see SAT02 notes).
questions.4.options.0.text.back: Melaka in the 1400s, in the sultanate period

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The sultanate came first, in the 1400s. The map was made about 90 years after the Portuguese took the city. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The sultanate came first, in the 1400s. This map was made about 90 years after the Portuguese seized the town. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: Melaka in the time of Portuguese rule
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Melaka in the time the Portuguese ruled

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The Portuguese took Melaka in 1511, and the map comes from their time. It cannot show the city of the 1400s.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The Portuguese seized Melaka in 1511, and this map is from their time. It cannot show the town in the 1400s.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: Melaka today, as a heritage city
questions.4.options.2.text.back: Melaka today, as a heritage city

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The map is more than 400 years old. UNESCO's modern record tells us about Melaka today. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.note: UNESCO is written ยูเนสโก (the usual Thai spelling, and read aloud correctly), not kept in Latin letters. Used in quiz-memory-and-shared-histories too.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This map is more than 400 years old. It is UNESCO's modern record that tells us about Melaka today. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.5.question.source: The 1604 map shows a big fort, a river and roads. Whose view is hard to find on it?
questions.5.question.back: The 1604 map shows a large fort, a river and streets. Whose point of view is hard to find on this map?

questions.5.options.0.text.note: Second pass: mapmaker is นักทำแผนที่, as in SAT03 (was คนทำแผนที่).

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The map shows what the mapmaker chose to draw. It shows his perspective. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A map shows what the mapmaker chose to draw, so it shows his point of view. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.5.options.1.text.back: UNESCO's point of view on this city

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. UNESCO wrote about Melaka in modern times. That is a different source from the map. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. UNESCO wrote about Melaka in modern times. That is a different source from the map. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.5.options.2.text.back: The point of view of local people

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The map shows a fort and roads, but few homes or people at work. Their view is hard to find.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. The map shows a fort and streets but hardly any houses or people working, so their point of view is hard to find.

results.high.source: Well done. You can tell what an object or a map shows from what we guess about it.
results.high.back: Great work. You can tell what an object or map shows and what is our guess about it.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Well done. You got many right. Go back to the lessons for the questions you have not got right yet, then try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 1–3, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Go back to Lessons 1–3 and try again. Take as long as you need.
